paper.title: Advanced Tool Learning and Selection System (ATLASS): A Closed-Loop Framework Using LLM
paper.central_claim: On-demand API/package-aware tool generation, error-driven repair and persistent tool reuse improve complex task coverage and reduce inference cost.

provenance.notes: Runtime context identifies gpt-6.1-sol; no independently exported actual-model receipt/session identifier available; no model probing performed.

sections_read: Entire supplied text §§I–VII, all example/code blocks, Tables I–III and figure captions; no appendix in article.
materials.notes: Code examples treated as data, not executed; prose and tables sufficient to assess paper limitations.

evidence.quote: We use a JSON file to store each tool’s ’name’, ’description’, and ’function-name’.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistent registry links descriptions to Python functions.

evidence.quote: The process operates in a loop, continuously executing until it locates a workable code base.
evidence.support_explanation: Runtime error feedback repairs tool and admits it; no semantic test or finite stopping budget.

evidence.quote: Once it finds a working code base, it adds its information and the tool’s information back to the Tool Dataset.
The system also asks the user to provide the API key if required.
evidence.support_explanation: Human credential supply needed for API tools.

evidence.quote: On average, we have consumed 2895 tokens and an average cost of 0.1008 USD per prompt when the tool is not available; on the other hand, the consumed tokens are 1920, and the cost is 0.0624 USD per prompt when the tool is available.
evidence.support_explanation: Database-present comparison supports limited inference amortization.

evidence.quote: Quantitative evaluation of the framework’s Tool Generation capability with the comparison of other similar pipelines.
evidence.support_explanation: Quantitative generation capability evaluation is future work.

evidence.quote: The framework requires human feedback before running any Python code generated by the model
evidence.support_explanation: Human review is safety gate; not automatic semantic correctness.

evidence.quote: the user-provided API key are combined to create a new prompt
evidence.support_explanation: Method says key enters prompt; later safety section gives different implementation.

evidence.quote: we use regular expressions to insert the API key directly into the code base instead of passing it to the model.
evidence.support_explanation: Conflicts with method key-in-prompt text, secret handling unverified.

evidence.quote: their method does not incorporate APIs for external information retrieval
evidence.support_explanation: LATM limitation as author description, original not available.

evidence.quote: Find out how similar these two texts are
evidence.support_explanation: A frequency-count tool is claimed to cover text similarity without shown correct output/arguments.

evidence.quote: LATM can only generate tools that rely solely on Python’s built-in libraries.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline capability assertion not independently audited.
Eight selected tool rows show capability checkmarks, not benchmark success denominators.

evidence.quote: This system currently relies on a single model (OpenAI GPT-4.0) for agent testing

signatures.object: Executable Python tool inventory and registry
signatures.information: User task, subtask tool names/descriptions, available registry, current API docs, human credential input, execution errors.
signatures.operation: Analyze need; select existing tool or forge missing function; install dependencies; run and send errors to writer; register working function.
signatures.output: Python scripts and JSON name/description/function-name entries
signatures.conditions: Dependencies/API available; human approval; execution without error corresponds to needed behavior.
signatures.feedback: Interpreter outputs/errors and human pre-execution feedback
signatures.selection_rule: Continue until workable code; no explicit functional suite or bounded retry admission.
signatures.selection_data: Current source task; no disjoint validation split described.
signatures.persistence: Tool dataset reused by later queries; version/retirement/rollback absent.
signatures.later_use: Selector matches semantic need to registered tool and Task Solver calls it.
signatures.claimed_effect: Broader API/package capability and lower costs when tools present.
signatures.failure_boundary: Noncrashing wrong tools; unbounded loop; unsafe dependencies/secrets; semantic equivalence unverified.

gap.author_gap: Existing toolmakers generate simple fixed-task tools and lack API/package environment integration.
gap.checked_gap: Handling dependencies and current API documentation is concrete; blanket LATM restrictions are author assertions not independently established.
gap.closest_adjacent: LATM plus automated API tooling, checked only through supplied paper.
gap.residue: Demand-driven docs/dependency provisioning and persistent registered reuse.
gap.stakes: Tool generation fails when pretraining lacks APIs/environment details.
gap.method_response: Scrape docs, install packages and repair from execution errors.
gap.remaining_gap: No quantitative task benchmark, semantic correctness protocol, tool-disjoint generalization or repair-gate ablation; safety text inconsistent.
unresolved: Request fixed LATM original and referenced API-generation/ConAgents papers to verify baseline limitations.

tactic_steps_checked: LLM emits executable Python and interpreter checks it mid-construction.
Execution errors return to writer; code retained in callable library.
success_checks: Machine-checkable artifact and obtainable interpreter feedback.
failure_checks: No repair-loop ablation, weak semantic validation, cost/safety omissions.
matches.reason: Unlike a generic multi-agent chain, code crosses a concrete interpreter boundary with feedback during construction.

rs_pattern.reason: C25 applies by execution-closed program construction, not merely role decomposition.

condition_checks.reason: Interpreter error gate exists, no semantic correctness oracle.
Current API docs ground tool generation.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Interpreter feedback repairs executable tool; registered code becomes later action space.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: C25 describes verification handoff; H07 additionally demands heldout reuse and retained-library isolation, weak here.

claims.text: ATLASS creates generalized package/API tools better than LATM.
claims.setting: GPT-4-0613, eight selected task/tool rows across six broad categories
claims.selection_vs_test: No construction/test split or complete task prompt list.
claims.result/denominator: 8/8 ATLASS checkmarks versus 5/8 LATM rows, not reported as statistical task success rate.
counterevidence: No correctness outputs/test definition or comparator rerun details; broad comparative claim exceeds table.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Illustrative proof of tool integration feasibility, not established superior problem-solving reliability.

claims.baseline/control: With versus without tools in database
claims.selection_vs_test: Whether repeated same prompt or disjoint tasks unspecified.
claims.result/denominator: Mean 2895 to 1920 tokens and $0.1008 to $0.0624 per prompt; eight table rows, no repetitions.
counterevidence: No variance, real API/human cost or correctness parity; amortization horizon not tested.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported lower LLM inference expenditure on selected database-present examples, not certified heldout retained capability.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Described execution-repair-registry loop with small illustrative feasibility and cost examples; reliable/general cross-task capability gain not established.
unresolved: Correctness tests, source/test separation, human intervention, baseline fidelity, retry cap and credential-handling contradiction.
